MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  NOVEMBER 18, 2019

  The Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at 7:07
  p.m. at City Council Chambers 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California
  by CHAIR RETZ.

  1.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR RETZ led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Retz, Persichina, Romanelli, Pope, Ciarolla, Bain &
  McCormick

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  None

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager
  Mike Goldsmith, Maintenance Superintendent
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor
  Daniel A-Haja, Comm. Services Coordinator

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF OCTOBER 21, 2019

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted one correction to the minutes to correct a spelling error of
  Dale Allen’s name on page four.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE
  to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 21, 2019 AS CORRECTED

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  B.  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL AND PARK & ACTIVITES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 22, 2019 (CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING)

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted that for consistency purposes, she would like her last
  name to appear as POPE rather than VAN INGEN POPE in these minutes and all
  minute records going forward.
  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI to:

PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
NOVEMBER 18, 2019
   APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 22, 2019 (CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEFING) AS CORRECTED

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  4.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  None

  5.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  STREET TREE REMOVAL APPLICATION PROCESS

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a brief overview per the agenda
  material.

  Commission discussion ensued. CHAIR RETZ suggested that the homeowner be allowed
  to bring their application to the commission if requested and that there be consideration of
  powerlines. He further suggested that the application be updated to reflect if trees are
  impacting electrical lines.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked what type of requests would receive staff approval
  and wondered if it would include regular impacts to sewer lines. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith affirmed and added that historically removal is approved if there
  is impact to a sidewalk.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if the intent of this proposal was to streamline the
  tree removal process. Goldsmith affirmed. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI additionally
  asked if “unique circumstances” should be defined.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA explained that historically the Commission would do site
  visits to every tree removal request and over time realized the criteria was often the same
  which allowed approval, but stated that he does not want administrative approval for view
  issues. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith explained that views are considered only
  for tree trimming purposes, maintaining the health of the tree. He further explained that
  an applicant request for tree removal simply for view reasons would need to be considered
  by the Commission.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if the application can be updated to recommend
  the reason for the request by providing the applicant with options. CHAIR RETZ added
  that if the request is related to damage, it should be administratively reviewed; whereas if
  the application does not suggest damage or there is light damage as a result of the tree,
  the Commission should review it. He further suggested that the application include any
  impact as a result to adjacent to powerlines.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE
  to:

DPARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 18, 2019
   PERMIT STAFF APPROVAL OF CITY STREET TREE REMOVALS AND
  REPLACEMENTS REQUESTS UPON CRITERIA RELATED TO DAMAGE DONE
  BY THE TREE; COMMISSION TO REVIEW APPLICATIONS WITH UNIQUE
  CIRCUMSTANCES, SUCH AS LITTLE OR NO DAMAGE CAUSED BY THE
  TREE AND VIEW IMPACTS; UPDATE THE APPLICATION TO PROVIDE
  APPLICANT OPTIONS OF REASONS OF THE REQUEST, INCLUDING THE
  POTENTIAL IMPACT OF POWERLINES,

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  B.  PORTUGUESE BEND NATIONAL HORSE SHOW (PBNHS) REQUEST

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith provided a brief overview per the agenda
  material.

  CHAIR RETZ asked if there is a schedule when this proposed work would be done as part
  of a regular City project. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith explained that the City
  does complete annual maintenance but this work is removing the footing completely and
  adding material, laser grade and everything back packed which benefits all equestrians
  using the arena, as well as staff because it requires less maintenance during the rainy
  season.

  Assistant City Manager Davis noted that the Equestrian Committee approved PBNHS
  proposal at its meet held earlier in the evening.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA provided an overview of the Equestrian Committee
  discussion explaining that PBNHS requested that if the work completed was closer to
  $20,000, they may ask for consideration of a partial or full waiver of a third year of event
  fees.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA CHAIR RETZ asked if the work could be put out to bid.
  Assistant City Manager Davis responded that based upon the dollar amount a formal bid
  would not be needed. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith added that the service
  provider has experience in this type of footing work, is highly recommended by local horse
  shows and has completed work for the city in the past.

  CHAIR RETZ asked when this work would be completed. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that it could be completed in a matter of weeks upon City Council
  approval and that work should begin before the rainy season affects the horse rings.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if the money received by the PBNHS is crucial to our
  budget and whether a grant could cover the ring renovation rather than having PBNHS
  pay for it. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded saying that the ring
  renovation was not a budgeted item. Assistant City Manager Davis added that the
  proposed renovation goes beyond standard maintenance, and that grant options have not
  been explored. Although the PBNHS is a large event and not receiving the fees would
  impact the budget, City staff could adjust accordingly.

PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 18, 2019
   COMMISSIONER BAIN asked how the event fees from PBNHS are used. Assistant City
  Manager Davis responded that the fall within the City’s General Fund.

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith stated that as the rains affect the horse arenas,
  material is lost over time which need to be replaced at the proper level. The proposed
  renovation by PBNHS would reduce the amount replaced during the rainy season.
  Assistant City Manager Davis added that the approximate $6,000 would not be detrimental
  to the City’s budget if not received as the renovation would save in future arena
  maintenance cost and staff time.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked what the amount of dollars to offset the cost of the
  proposed renovation would have on the City’s General fund. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith responded that the cost of yearly fillings and staff time would be saved with the
  renovation.

  Assistant City Manager Davis added that the Commission could consider waiving a portion
  of the fees and not match dollar for dollar against the cost of the renovation.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked for clarification of the quote of work and why the range is
  from $14,000 to $20,000. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it
  depends upon how much additional material may be needed.

  CHAIR RETZ stated that he would be comfortable with waiving the fees for one or two
  years.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about how the proposed work would address
  safety concerns of the arenas. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that in
  the dry season the rings are fine but the wet season still have some damp rings. This can
  cause uneven footing for horses. He added that this time between horse show seasons
  would also be a beneficial time to start the renovation project as it also misses rainy
  season.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted that Ring 5 was renovated in the past but no longer
  used. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that the proposed renovations
  of rings 3 and 4 are in higher demand as they are used more frequently.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI would like to finalize the agreement and would not include
  the third year of waived fees for any unforeseen increase in cost.

  COMMISSIONER POPE would not like the agreement to go beyond two years and asked
  if PBNHS paid this year’s 2019 event fees. Assistant City Manager Davis responded that
  staff was asked by PBNHS to take the issue to the Commission before payment of fees.

  COMMISSIONER POPE requested that further research in cost savings and benefits be
  provided. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA stated that the safety of the horses and the riders
  are affected by the condition of the riding rings and renovations could help to prevent
  injury.

PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 18, 2019
   COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK stated that it should be the City’s responsibility to make
  the rings as safe as possible.

  CHAIR RETZ asked how long the arenas would be down if the renovation were to proceed.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that it would take one week to
  renovate the rings.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked what would happen if the renovation costs would cover a
  third year of fees. Assistant City Manager Davis responded that if the job is over $14,000
  then the overage would be donated to the City.

  CHAIR RETZ asked if this cost was reasonable. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith
  affirmed explaining that the renovation will be precise and laser-graded and will be
  overseen by City Staff.

  Assistant City Manager Davis added that further details of the renovation would be in an
  agreement with PBNHS with approval by the City Attorney.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted that ideally a response from the Commission
  should take place before the rainy season.

  COMMSSIONER BAIN recommends that the City waive fees of two years only.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI recommends that the work not exceed the cost of
  $23,000.

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  RECOMMEND APPROVAL TO THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE PORTUGUESE
  BEND NATIONAL HORSE SHOW REQUEST TO PAY FOR IMPROVEMENTS
  TO ARENAS 3 AND 4 AT ERNIE HOWLETT WITH TWO YEARS OF EVENT
  FEES WAIVED; PROJECT WORK SHOULD NOT EXCEED $23,000; CITY
  ATTORNEY TO CRAFT LANGUAGE THAT WILL BE ACCEPTABLE FOR CITY
  COUNCIL APPROVAL; IF PBNHS REQUESTS A THIRD YEAR OF EVENT FEES
  BE WAIVED, THE REQUEST SHOULD RETURN TO THE COMMISSION;
  FINANCIAL ANALYSIS TO THE CITY COUNCIL SHOULD INCLUDE MATERIAL
  AND STAFF COSTS

  CHAIR RETZ REQUESTED A ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Ciarolla, Bain, Persichina, Retz, Pope, McCormick, Romanelli
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  6.  AUDJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATON ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  A.  NEW PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION LOGO

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a brief overview per the agenda material.

PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 18, 2019
   COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK considered the new alternative logo options to be more
  focused on the Pepper Tree and did not demonstrate the purpose of the Foundation.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN approved of the original logo image as revised.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to:

  RECOMMEND THE ORIGINAL REVISED PEPPER TREE LOGO FOR
  APPROVAL BY THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE PEPPER TREE
  FOUNDATION.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  B.  HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a brief overview confirming the
  Parade Grand Marshal Allison Compton, Community Grand Marshalls Pat Barrett-Hill and
  Jim Hill, and Hometown Grand Marshall Dale Allen. Sponsors of the event were also
  confirmed included Malaga Bank, Code Ninjas, Rolling Hills Dental Group, Bennett
  Landscaping, and Cal Water. In-kind donations are provided by Starbucks, El Pollo Inka,
  and the Chamber of Commerce. Pre-recorded interviews will also be taking place later
  this week with Manhattan Beach Studios along with the sending out of Pre Parade
  reception invitations. Live streaming and additional lighting were also added to this year’s
  event.

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated Highridge Park has a couple issues such as gopher holes
  and a sink hall near back portion of trail. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith reported
  that a main line had blown out over the weekend but staff is addressing the issue.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN added that the left side sink of the Women’s restroom did not
  work at Highridge Park and it needed to be cleaned. Trash was also overflowing and not
  properly sorted. Assistant City Manager Davis responded that the Big Belly trash cans are
  supposed to be self-compacting and that contact with Waste Management will be made
  to resolve the issue. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith added that a count of the
  rolling totes have been made at the park and that they will be replaced with cleaner ones.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if a possible sonar system could be used to deter gophers.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that staff will look into the use of sonar.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if some painting could be done in the back fencing of the
  park as it is starting to look used. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that
  the fencing will be getting replaced with wood fencing as the vinyl fencing does not hold
  up to patron use.

PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 18, 2019
   COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that trash bins at Rockbluff Park indicated alcohol
  consumption. He added that now some trash bins are missing from the park. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that staff took away the bins to get replaced.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that this issue has been brought to the attention of
  Judy Bayer, the Rockbluff HOA President. Assistant City Manager Davis noted the
  Sheriff’s Department could be contacted to make more frequent drive by checks of the
  park.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK noted trash at George F Canyon trail. Branches are also
  encroaching on the trail. Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that staff will
  take care of the issue.

  CHAIR RETZ noted that some trails adjacent to the golf course has water leaking down
  the trail. The trail at the Nature Preserve near Buckskin and Dapplegray Lane has an old
  fence post that may be a hazard for horse riders. The trail behind Buckskin has railroad
  ties that have exposed pieces of rebar that may also injure horses on the trail.
  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith responded that staff will assess the areas.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  HOLIDAY ACTIVITIES (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a brief overview. Staff would give
  the opportunity for children to send a letter to Santa through the upcoming newsletter and
  Santa would be able to send them a response by the Holiday. The nominal cost would
  include postage and stationary. The Promenade on the Peninsula will also partner with
  the City to schedule pet photos with Santa.

  The adopt a family program will also be taken up this year in partnership with the Lomita
  Fire Station and Fire Station 106 to host a box donation at their respective locations.
  Assistant City Manager Davis also added that two families have been adopted this year
  and that invitations to the City Holiday Party will be sent out shortly.

  CHAIR RETZ asked if the letters to Santa would need a vote by the Commission as it may
  cost money. Assistant City Manager Davis responded that it may be approved by the
  Commission but that the letters fall within the City Manager’s authority within the budget.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked how families can send the letters out. Community
  Services Supervisor Morquecho responded that letters could be mailed or dropped off at
  City Hall and that a short prompt by the newsletter will allow for more standardized
  responses from the City Staff.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked if an update can be provided at the next
  commission meeting.

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
NOVEMBER 18, 2019
   A.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTIONS OF OCTOBER 22, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING ACTIOINS OF NOVEMBER 12, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  2020 SPONSORSHIP PACKAGE

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted that staff is working on creating an
  annual sponsorship package. COMMISSIONER POPE noted that ideally the package
  should be sent out earlier as most companies set their budget before January.

  B.  SPECIAL EVENT ORDINANCE

  Assistant City Manager Davis noted that Staff is working with the City Attorney to refine a
  special event permit code.

  C.  PROPOSED SUMMER MOVIE FILMS

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja noted that a list of proposed movies this year
  would include some teen or adult oriented films not to exceed the PG rating. The
  Commission discussed making sure there were still children-friendly movies in the mix.

  D.  RACE AGREEMENT REVIEW

  Community Services Supervisor Morquecho noted that Staff is currently working with the
  City Attorney to review and update the race agreement.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI wanted to follow up regarding possible mural at Highridge
  Park and also the automated lockers presented by the audience from the last meeting.
  Assistant City Manager Davis responded that staff has tried to follow up with Mariana
  Desalles but no response was given and that staff will continue to follow-up with her.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked the status of the automated lockers presented by
  the audience member at last month’s meeting; staff responded that the presenter has not
  yet been in touch with the City with further details.

  COMMISSIONER MCORMICK asked for an update with Butcher Park and what the
  budget would be from Cal Water. Assistant City Manager Davis noted that the budget is
  still in process.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about introducing a scenic lookout at the George
  F Canyon trail. Assistant City Manager Davis noted that staff can come back with a
  proposal.

PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
NOVEMBER 18, 2019
   11.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING AT 8:00 PM TO AN ADJOURNED PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES MEETING ON DECEMBER 16, 2019 AT 7:00 P.M. IN THE CITY
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4045 PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH, ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES.

  There being no objection, CHAIR RETZ so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,
